messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-314 noisy.synthetic-canary-latency (us-west-1) — threshold breached for 2m, count=7

sam.k: acked oncall

incident-bot: sam.k acknowledged the alert

mira: looking — pulling canary dashboard now. graphs show 95p latency spike coincident with synthetic job at 03:42:10 UTC

jon: same, no error-rate uptick on prod. only synthetic canaries (svc:canary-runner) spiking. possible test runner overload?

sam.k: can we confirm customer-facing routes are fine? quick check on /v1/generate 200s?

mira: checking traces — proxy latency increased, origin latency stable. suggests upstream queueing at gateway layer.

jon: adding @sre-rotation in case this escalates.

sre-rotation: on it, joining. quick grep of router logs shows repeated 503s to synthetic-runner pool around 03:42

opsbot: automated mitigation: temporarily rate-limit synthetic-canary traffic (rule: canary-runner -> rate_limit 10r/s) applied by opsbot user

sam.k: nice. did PD auto-escalate or stay within oncall? saw a couple duplicate pages earlier.

incident-bot: Duplicate suppression: 2 duplicate pages auto-collapsed. current page remains with active ack by sam.k

mira: after rate-limit, latency back to baseline within ~20s. canaries still running but below threshold.

jon: no user-facing impact confirmed. no major errors in errortracker.

sam.k: leaving notes in PD: "transient synthetic flood; rate-limited canary runner; no customer impact; monitor for 10m"

mira: quick postmortem checklist: 1) keep rate-limit for 10m 2) investigate why canary job concurrency spiked 3) consider backoff in canary runner 4) communicate to devtools team

jon: here's the command I ran to rate-limit (for audit):

```
opsctl traffic throttle set --service canary-runner --region us-west-1 --qps 10
```

sam.k: thanks. I'll stay watch for 10m then handoff to next oncall if clear. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: alert auto-resolved at 4250001257 (duration 23s) — marked resolved by incident-bot due to metric recovery

sre-rotation: quick note for runbook: add guidance to throttle synthetic traffic automatically on short spikes; we had safe fallback.

mira: filing an action item in #eng-sre: "investigate synthetic-runner concurrency spike" and pinging devtools.

sam.k: final: no customer impact, short PD noise, auto-resolved after mitigation. handoff to next oncall in 5m if stable.

jon: copying runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-flood (please update with recommended thresholds)

sre-rotation: acknowledged, will follow up during next blameless review.

sam.k: handing off to next oncall — leaving channel.

mira: thanks all, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
